parts.problem_md:
This question is about silicon and carbon.

Silicon is a semiconductor.

i) Data obtained using the mass spectrum of silicon are shown.

| **Isotope mass number** | **Relative abundance** |
|---|---|
| 28 | 92.17 |
| 29 | 4.71 |
| 30 | 3.12 |

Calculate the relative atomic mass of silicon to **two** decimal places.

**(2)**

ii) Suggest a reason why there is a small peak in the mass spectrum of silicon at *m / z *= 14

**(1)**

iii) Complete the table to show the number of protons and neutrons in each isotope of silicon.

| **Isotope** | **Number of protons** | **Number of neutrons** |
|---|---|---|
| <sup>28</sup>Si |   |   |
| <sup>29</sup>Si |   |   |
| <sup>30</sup>Si |   |   |

**(1)**
parts.solution_md:
i) The relative atomic mass of silicon to **two** decimal places is:

- *A*<sub>r</sub> = `fraction numerator open parentheses 28 space cross times space 92.17 close parentheses space plus space open parentheses 29 space cross times space 4.71 close parentheses space plus space open parentheses 30 space cross times space 3.12 close parentheses over denominator 100 end fraction` = 28.1095; **[1 mark]**
- To two decimal places: = 28.11; **[1 mark]**

ii) A reason why there is a small peak in the mass spectrum of silicon at *m / z *= 14 is:

- Some silicon atoms (of mass 28) lose two electrons / have a charge of 2+; **[1 mark]**

iii) The completed table is:

| **Isotope** | **Number of protons** | **Number of neutrons** |
|---|---|---|
| <sup>28</sup>Si | **Final answer:** **14** | **Final answer:** **14** |
| <sup>29</sup>Si | **Final answer:** **14** | **Final answer:** **15** |
| <sup>30</sup>Si | **Final answer:** **14** | **Final answer:** **16** |

- All values correct; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *Ensure you give calculated values to the required number of decimal places - this is an easy mark to lose!*
- *A correct value for **A*<sub>*r*</sub>* scores 2 marks without working*
- *The only acceptable units for **A*<sub>*r*</sub>* are g mol*<sup>*-1*</sup>* or a.m.u. *
- *If you obtain a value between 28 and 30 but the expression used is incorrect, you would score 1 mark*
- *Remember**: The peaks on a mass spectrum occur at **m** / **z** values, which is the mass to charge ratio*
- *In most cases, the charge is +1, so the **m** / **z** value is just the mass of the ion*
- *In this case, the **m** / z value for the Si*<sup>*2+*</sup>* ion is 28 / 2 = 14*

**(1)**

parts.problem_md:
Silicon dioxide, SiO<sub>2</sub> , is the main constituent of sand and has a giant lattice structure similar to that of diamond.

![q13b-paper-1-oct-2021-edexcel-ial-chemistry](assets/004-q13b-paper-1-oct-2021-edexcel-ial-chemistry.png)

Crystalline silicon dioxide is used on the surface of semiconductor devices to provide a heat-resistant, electrically insulating layer.

Explain how the structure and bonding of silicon dioxide make it useful for this application.
parts.solution_md:
The structure and bonding of silicon dioxide make it useful for a heat-resistant, electrically insulating layers because:

- **All **atoms are joined together by covalent bonds / giant covalent (structure);** [1 mark]**
- These are strong / take a lot of energy to break (so melting temperature is very high); **[1 mark]**
- No electrons are free (to move) / mobile / delocalised / (so charge cannot be carried); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *There are two properties that make silicon dioxide useful in this application:*

  - *High melting temperature so it can withstand heat*
  - *Non-conductor of electricity so it can act as an electrical insulator*
- *Whenever referring to the properties of substances, you must explain how the bonds / forces within the structure give rise to these properties*
- *You are told that silicon dioxide has a similar structure to diamond, so the same explanations from the properties of diamond can be applied to silicon dioxide*

  - *There are no intermolecular forces, just strong covalent bonds between all of the atoms which require a large amount of energy to overcome, giving it a high melting temperature*
  
    - *You would not be given credit if you refer to a high boiling temperature as this is not relevant in this application*
  - *All of the outer electrons of silicon and oxygen are involved in bonding so there are no free electrons to carry charge*

parts.problem_md:
Calcium silicate is formed in the removal of silicon dioxide impurities in the extraction of iron from its ores. A sample of calcium silicate composed of calcium, silicon and oxygen was found to contain 12.0 g of calcium, 8.43 g of silicon and 14.47 g of oxygen.

Determine the empirical formula of calcium silicate. You **must** show your working.
parts.solution_md:
The empirical formula of calcium silicate is:

- Calculation of number of moles: $\mathrm{Ca}:\frac{12}{40.1}\mathrm{Si}:\frac{8.43}{28.1}O:\frac{14.47}{16}$ 
**OR**
Ca : Si : O = 0.299 : 0.30 : 0.904; **[1 mark]**
- Calculation of whole number mole ratio: 1 : 1 : 3; **[1 mark]**
- Empirical formula: CaSiO<sub>3</sub>; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *To find the whole number ratio, divide the number of moles of each element by the smallest number of moles*
- *It is a common mistake for students to forget to give the empirical formula once they have calculated the whole number ratio - a frustrating mark to lose when the hard work has been done!*

parts.problem_md:
Carbon dioxide is a gas at room temperature. A fizzy drink is canned at 5.0°C and 1.3 × 10<sup>5 </sup>Pa and contains approximately 3 g of carbon dioxide.

Calculate the volume, in cm<sup>3</sup>, occupied by 3.00 g of carbon dioxide gas at 5.0°C and 1.3 × 10<sup>5 </sup>Pa.

[*pV = nRT*     R = 8.31 Jmol<sup>−1</sup>K<sup>−1</sup>]
parts.solution_md:
The volume, in cm<sup>3</sup>, occupied by 3.00 g of carbon dioxide gas at 5.0 °C and 1.3 × 10<sup>5 </sup>Pa is:

- Calculation of moles carbon dioxide: 3 ÷ 44 = 0.06818;** [1 mark]**
- Conversion of temperature to K: 273 + 5 = 278; **[1 mark]**
- Rearrangement of expression: *V *= $\frac{nRT}{p}=\frac{0.06818\times8.31\times278}{1.3\times10^{5}}$ (= 1.2116 x 10<sup>-3</sup> m<sup>3</sup>); **[1 mark]**
- Evaluation of answer in cm<sup>3</sup>: = 1211.6 / 1212 / 1210 /1200 (cm<sup>3</sup>); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *The most common mistakes made with these types of calculations are not converting / incorrectly converting to the correct units and not rearranging the expression correctly*
- *To convert from m*<sup>*3*</sup>* to cm*<sup>*3*</sup>*, multiply by 10*<sup>*6*</sup>
- *If you are not confident in rearranging, it can be best to substitute values into the equation **pV** = **nRT **first:*

  - *1.3 x 10*<sup>*5*</sup>* x **V** = 0.06818 x 8.31 x 278*
- *Then simplify:*

  - *1.3 x 10*<sup>*5*</sup>* x **V** = 157.508*
- *Then rearrange:*

  - *V** = *$\frac{157.508}{1.3\times10^{5}}$* = 1.2116 x 10*<sup>*-3 *</sup>*m*<sup>*3*</sup>

parts.problem_md:
A 0.210 g sample of a volatile organic liquid **C** is injected into a gas syringe and heated in an oven. At 100 kPa and 358 K, the syringe contains 72.5 cm<sup>3 </sup>of gas.

Calculate the molar mass of **C**. 
[*pV = nRT        R* = 8.31 J mol<sup>−1</sup> K<sup>−1</sup> ]
parts.solution_md:
The molar mass of **C **is:

- Conversion of volume to m<sup>3</sup> 72.5 × 10<sup>-6</sup> = 7.25 × 10<sup>-5</sup> / 0.0000725 (m<sup>3</sup>); **[1 mark]**
- Rearrangement of Ideal Gas Equation *n =* $\frac{pV}{RT}$; **[1 mark]**
- Conversion of pressure and evaluation to give number of moles $\frac{100000\times7.25x10^{-5}}{8.31\times358}$= 2.4370 × 10<sup>− 3</sup> / 0.002437(mol); **[1 mark]**
- Calculation of molar mass $\frac{0.210}{2.4370\times10^{-3}}=$86.172 = 86 (g mol<sup>-1</sup>); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *You must know the ideal gas equation, **pV **= **nRT **and be able to rearrange it*
- *Don't forget that units for volume and pressure should be m*<sup>*3*</sup>* and Pa respectively *

  - *To convert from cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* to m*<sup>*3*</sup>* divide 72.5 by 1 000 000*
  - *To convert from kPa to Pa, multiply 100 by 1000*
- *Once the number of moles have been calculated, use *$\frac{\mathrm{mass}}{\mathrm{number} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{moles}}$* to find the molar mass of **C*

parts.solution_md:

parts.problem_md:
Arsine is a reducing agent and reacts with cerium(IV) sulfate solution, forming arsenic.

The data from an experiment are shown.

Volume of arsine gas = 350 cm<sup>3</sup> at 115000 Pa and 20 °C

Volume of cerium(IV) sulfate solution = 488 cm<sup>3 </sup>

Concentration of cerium(IV) sulfate solution = 0.102 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>

i) Complete the half‐equation.

**(1)**

AsH<sub>3</sub> → As

ii) Calculate the final oxidation state of the cerium ion formed in the reaction.

**(6)**
parts.solution_md:
i) The completed half equation is:

- AsH<sub>3</sub> → As + 3H<sup>+</sup> + 3e(<sup>−</sup>); **[1 mark] **

ii) To calculate the final oxidation state of the cerium ion formed in the reaction:

- Moles of Ce<sup>4+</sup> $\frac{488}{1000}\times0.102$ = 0.049776 (mol);** [1 mark] **
- Calculation of *T* in *K *and *V* in m<sup>3</sup> *T* = 293 K 
**AND **
*V* =** **350 × 10<sup>−6</sup> m<sup>3</sup>;** [1 mark] **
- Rearrangement of* pV = nRT* *n* = $\frac{PV}{RT}$; **[1 mark] **
- Calculation of *n *for arsine *n* = $\frac{115000\times350\times10^{-6}}{8.31\times293}$ = 0.016531; **[1 mark] **
- Deduction of whole number ratio of AsH<sub>3</sub> : Ce<sup>4+</sup> $\frac{0.049776}{0.016531}$ = 1 : 3;** [1 mark] **
- The oxidation state of cerium in the product = Ce<sup>3+</sup> / (+)3; **[1 mark] **

**Final answer:** **[Total: 7 marks] **

- *The first step is to calculate the number of moles of Ce*<sup>*4+*</sup>* by using moles = volume (dm*<sup>*3*</sup>*) x concentration *

  - *If you use volume in cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* then you must divide by 1000*
- *Conversion of units for the **PV** = **nRT** equation is essential*

  - *To convert the temperature from °C to K, you add 273*
  - *To convert the volume from cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* to m*<sup>*3*</sup>*, you divide by 10*<sup>*6*</sup>
  - *Pressure is given to you in Pa, so there is no need to change this*
- *You will score a mark for rearranging the equation to find **n*
- *The ratio between the number of moles of arsine and Ce*<sup>*4+*</sup>* will give the oxidation state of Ce*<sup>*3+*</sup>* in the product *
- *This is because we need to multiply the half equation for the reduction of Ce4+ by 3 to form a full equation *

  - *Ce*<sup>*4+*</sup>* + e*<sup>*-*</sup>* → Ce*<sup>*3+*</sup>* (x3)*
  - *AsH*<sub>*3*</sub>* → As + 3H*<sup>*+*</sup>* + 3e*<sup>*−*</sup>
  - *AsH*<sub>*3 *</sub>*+ 3Ce*<sup>*4+*</sup>* → As + 3Ce*<sup>*3+*</sup>* *

parts.problem_md:
The maximum permitted concentration of sulfur in diesel fuel is 10 mg of sulfur in 1 kg of diesel fuel.

What is this concentration of sulfur in ppm?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** because:**

- To calculate the concentration in ppm:

  - $\frac{\mathrm{mass} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{sulfur}}{\mathrm{mass} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{diesel} \mathrm{fuel}}\times1000000$
- The mass of the sulfur and diesel must be in the same units:

  - Mass of sulfur in grams = 10 x 10<sup>-3</sup> g
  - Mass of diesel in grams = 1000 g
- Therefore, concentration = $\frac{10\times10^{-3}}{1000}\times1000000=10\mathrm{ppm}$

**A** is incorrect as  this is the ratio by mass

**B** is incorrect as  in the mass ratio the unit of kg has been ignored and this is based on 10 mg of sulfur in 1 g of fuel

**D** is incorrect as  this is based on 10 g of sulfur in 1 kg of fuel

parts.problem_md:
3.2 kg of this diesel fuel is burned in air.

What is the maximum volume, in dm<sup>3</sup>, of sulfur dioxide which can be produced, measured at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.)?

[Molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24 dm<sup>3</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup>]
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** because:**

- 3.2 kg of diesel fuel contains 3.2 x 10 = 32 mg = 32 x 10<sup>-3</sup> g of sulfur
- Moles of sulfur = $\frac{\mathrm{mass}}{M_{r}}=\frac{32\times10^{-3}}{32.1}=9.9688...\times10^{-4}$ moles
- The equation when sulfur combusts is

  - S + O<sub>2</sub> → SO<sub>2</sub>
- Therefore 9.9688... x 10<sup>-4 </sup>moles of sulfur dioxide is produced
- Volume of sulfur dioxide = moles x 24 = 9.9688... x 10<sup>-4</sup> x 24 = 0.024 dm<sup>3</sup>

**B** is incorrect as the molar mass of sulfur has not been taken into account

**C** is incorrect as  the mass ratio has been ignored

**D** is incorrect as the units of mg have been ignored

parts.problem_md:
A mass of 4.179 g of hydrated iron(III) sulfate, Fe<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>·H<sub>2</sub>O, was dissolved in deionised water and the solution made up to 200 cm<sup>3 .</sup>

What is the concentration of sulfate ions, SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>, in the solution, in mol dm<sup>−3</sup>?

[Molar mass of Fe<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>·H<sub>2</sub>O = 417.9 g mol<sup>−1</sup>]

**Final answer:** **The answer is**** D ****because:**

parts.problem_md:
c) The sodium hydroxide solution was neutralised with sulfuric acid.

Which is the ionic equation for this reaction?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** because:**

- The full equation for the neutralisation of sodium hydroxide with sulfuric acid is:

  - 2H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (aq) + 2NaOH<sup> </sup>(aq) → Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (aq) + 2H<sub>2</sub>O (l)
- Breaking the reactants and products down into their respective ions:

  - 2H<sup>+ </sup>(aq) + SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> (aq) + 2Na<sup>+ </sup>(aq) + 2OH<sup>− </sup>(aq) → 2Na<sup>+ </sup>(aq) + SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup> (aq) + 2H<sub>2</sub>O (l)
- Cancel out the spectator ions:

  - 2H<sup>+ </sup>(aq) + **SO**<sub>**4**</sub><sup>**2-**</sup>** (aq)** + **2Na**<sup>**+ **</sup>**(aq)** + 2OH<sup>− </sup>(aq) → **2Na**<sup>**+ **</sup>**(aq)** + **SO**<sub>**4**</sub><sup>**2-**</sup>** (aq)** + 2H<sub>2</sub>O (l)
  - 2H<sup>+ </sup>(aq) + 2OH<sup>− </sup>(aq) →  2H<sub>2</sub>O (l)
- Simplify:

  - H<sup>+ </sup>(aq) + OH<sup>− </sup>(aq) →  H<sub>2</sub>O (l)

**B** is incorrect as the water has been ignored

**C** is incorrect as  the sulfuric acid has not been shown as ions

**D** is incorrect as all the ions are shown but none are cancelled

parts.problem_md:
Sodium hydroxide solution was added to magnesium sulfate solution. The equation for the reaction is shown.

2NaOH(aq) + MgSO<sub>4</sub>(aq) → Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub>(s) + Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>(aq)

What is the atom economy (by mass) for the production of magnesium hydroxide?

[A<sub>r</sub> values: H = 1.0 O = 16.0 Na = 23.0 Mg = 24.3 S = 32.1]
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** because:**

- The atom economy is calculated by:

  - $\mathrm{Atom} \mathrm{economy}=\frac{M_{r}\mathrm{of} \mathrm{desired} \mathrm{produ}c\mathrm{ts}}{\mathrm{Sum} \mathrm{of}M_{r}\mathrm{of} \mathrm{ALL} \mathrm{reactants}}\times100$
- *M*<sub>r</sub>(Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub> = 24.3 + 2 x (16 + 1) = 58.3
- *M*<sub>r</sub>(NaOH) = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40
- *M*<sub>r</sub>(MgSO<sub>4</sub>) = 24.3 + 32.1 + (4 x 16) = 120.4
- Therefore:

  - $\frac{\mathrm{volume} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{nitrogen} \mathrm{dioxide}}{\mathrm{volume} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{air}}\times100$

- Percentage of nitrogen dioxide = $\frac{0.5}{1000000}$ x 100 = 0.00005%

parts.problem_md: Which aqueous solution has the **highest** concentration, in mol dm<sup>-3</sup>, of chloride ions?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** because:**

- To calculate the concentration in mol dm<sup>-3</sup> from g dm<sup>-3</sup>, divide by the* M*<sub>r</sub>:
- 0.1 g dm<sup>-3</sup> HCl = $\frac{0.1}{1+35.5}$ = 0.00274 mol dm<sup>-3</sup>

  - 1 mol of HCl releases 1 mol Cl<sup>-</sup> therefore the concentration of Cl<sup>-</sup> = **0.00274** mol dm<sup>-3</sup>
- 0.1 g dm<sup>-3</sup> NaCl = $\frac{0.1}{23+35.5}$ = 0.00171 mol dm<sup>-3</sup>

  - 1 mol of NaCl releases 1 mol Cl<sup>-</sup> therefore the concentration of Cl<sup>-</sup> = ** 0.00171** mol dm<sup>-3</sup>
- 0.1 g dm<sup>-3</sup> KCl = $\frac{0.1}{39.1+35.5}$ = 0.00134 mol dm<sup>-3</sup>

  - 1 mol of HCl releases 1 mol Cl<sup>-</sup> therefore the concentration of Cl<sup>-</sup> = **0.00134** mol dm<sup>-3</sup>
- 0.1 g dm<sup>-3</sup> BaCl<sub>2</sub> = `fraction numerator 0.1 over denominator 137.3 space plus space open parentheses 2 space cross times space 35.5 close parentheses end fraction` = 0.00048 mol dm<sup>-3</sup>

  - 1 mol of HCl releases 2 mol Cl<sup>-</sup> therefore the concentration of Cl<sup>-</sup> = **0.00096** mol dm<sup>-3</sup>
- The highest concentration of Cl<sup>-</sup> is in HCl, option **A**

**B**, **C** and **D** are incorrect as  HCl has a higher concentration of chloride ions

parts.problem_md:
A 4.00 mol dm<sup>−3</sup> solution of an acid is used to prepare dilute solutions of the acid.

What volume of water is required to make up 150 cm<sup>3</sup> of 0.35 mol dm<sup>−3</sup> solution of the acid?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** because:**

- The number of moles of acid in 150 cm<sup>3</sup> of 0.35 mol dm<sup>−3</sup> solution is $\frac{150}{1000}\times0.35$ = 0.0525 mol
- So the volume of acid required is $\frac{0.0525}{4}$ = 0.0131 dm<sup>3</sup> or 13.1 cm<sup>3</sup>
- If the total solution is 150 cm<sup>3</sup> and 13.1 cm<sup>3</sup> is acid the volume of water required is:

  - 150 - 13.1 = 136.9 cm<sup>3</sup>

**A** is incorrect as  this is the volume of acid required

**B** is incorrect as  this is the number of moles of acid multiplied by 1000

**C** is incorrect as  this is 150 ‒ (the number of moles of acid multiplied by 1000)
